description: Multi-phase plans currently in flight. Each phase references roadmap item ids; the activePhase section breaks the current phase into concrete tasks with status. Survives conversation compactions — a fresh session can pick up by reading this file.

phases.title: Foundation
phases.notes: Schema, bus, episodic memory, agent base. Nothing alive yet — just the substrate everything else hangs off.

phases.title: First Voice
phases.notes: Cheshire Cat end-to-end. Talking to himself. Layered context composer + engagement policy + ADR writer come online here because the Cat is their first consumer.

phases.title: First Tension
phases.notes: Add the White Rabbit. Two voices, role tension, semantic + relational memory layers populated as the agents accumulate history. Compaction-as-behavior arrives because it has to.

phases.title: First Race
phases.notes: Dodo orchestrator + quiescence + conflict resolution + first showcase (/health endpoint). The system runs end-to-end on a trivial directive. Init CLI lands here so the showcase can run against a real target project.

phases.title: Full Cast
phases.notes: Bring the rest of the cast online with integration tests per agent. Per-character artifact handlers for the new speech act payloads. Synthetic-consensus guard goes here because it only matters once disagreement is real.

phases.title: Real Threads
phases.notes: The hard showcases — translation chat MVP, security recovery, multi-session persistence. Transcript annotation tooling lets us publish them. Token telemetry confirms the engagement_policy is paying for itself.

phases.title: Evals
phases.notes: Generic-baseline vs Wonderland comparison. The compounding-curve plot is the legibility-of-value mitigation from §11. Without this the philosophy stays assertion.

activePhase.title: First Tension
activePhase.goal: The White Rabbit comes online; first inter-agent tension becomes observable. By end of P3, the Cat and Rabbit dance on the same thread — Cat reframes architecture, Rabbit decomposes into tickets, neither crosses domain. Semantic + relational memory layers persist agent-shaped distillations; compaction-as-agent-behavior runs between threads. Each character's relational notes update from real interactions, and those updates change subsequent behavior.
activePhase.sequencing: Ticket writer + registry first (mirrors T10 ADR pattern; gives the Rabbit somewhere to leave his pocket-watch marks). Then the Rabbit agent itself. Then a two-agent integration test — mocked for assertions, live-gated for showcase. Memory layers + AgentMemory composite + base-agent rewires last in the substrate ladder so they're proven by the time compaction reasons over them. Compaction is the closeout: agents reflect on threads in-character, distill semantic + relational notes for next time. Order: infrastructure → second voice → tension → memory → compaction.

tasks.title: Ticket writer + registry
tasks.details: src/wonderland/ticket.py — TicketPayload (Pydantic) matching white_rabbit.md §V (sources, owner, tier, estimate, dependencies, description, acceptance, risk). TicketStatus, TicketRecord, TicketRegistry. Files at <project_root>/.wonderland/tickets/ticket-NNN-slug.md. Looser validation than ADRs — tickets evolve more than ADRs do, so estimates can be vague-but-required, dependencies can be empty, acceptance can be a single bullet. Mirrors T10 structure; not a copy.
tasks.resolution: src/wonderland/ticket.py mirrors T10 ADR pattern. TicketTier (v1/fast-follow/post-launch), TicketStatus (open/in_flight/blocked/done/dropped), TicketDependencies (blocks/blocked_by/soft per Rabbit §V), TicketPayload with required title+owner+tier+estimate+description (the Rabbit always estimates — non-negotiable per §I), TicketRecord, TicketRegistry. Files at <project_root>/.wonderland/tickets/ticket-NNN-slug.md. Looser validation than ADRs — tickets evolve more, so dependencies/acceptance/risk default-empty rather than required. render_ticket produces markdown matching white_rabbit.md §V. Reuses adr.slugify (no need to duplicate). Risk section omitted from output when empty (clean rendering). Acceptance shows '(to be filled)' placeholder when empty so the Rabbit knows what's missing. 31 ticket tests; 258 total pass; ruff clean.

tasks.title: White Rabbit agent
tasks.details: src/wonderland/agents/white_rabbit.py — WhiteRabbit(WonderlandAgent) subclass. Loads constitutions/white_rabbit.md. white_rabbit_rules() encodes §III. RabbitResponse JSON protocol with decision (ticket/concern/question/reframe/deference/silence), body, and optional tickets[] array (one Rabbit turn can issue multiple tickets). Tickets persist through T12 registry. Mocked deliberate tests + 1 live smoke gated WONDERLAND_LLM_SMOKE.

tasks.title: Two-agent integration: Cat + Rabbit
tasks.details: tests/test_two_agent.py — bus + episodic stores + Cat + Rabbit + directive. Mocked LLMs for assertions (Cat asks reframing question, Rabbit issues a holding-pattern ticket and waits for architecture, Cat proposes, Rabbit decomposes proposal into tickets that reference it). Verify role boundaries — no Cat-tickets in published utterances, no Rabbit-proposals. Live integration smoke (gated) runs the same dance against Haiku 4.5 and captures the transcript for analyses/002.

tasks.title: Semantic + relational memory + AgentMemory composite
tasks.details: src/wonderland/memory/semantic.py — SemanticStore (markdown-backed: <project_root>/.wonderland/memory/<agent>/semantic/<topic>.md, plus optional SQLite index for queries). src/wonderland/memory/relational.py — RelationalStore (one markdown file per other agent at <project_root>/.wonderland/memory/<agent>/relational/<other_name>.md). Composite AgentMemory class wraps episodic + semantic + relational; replaces the bare EpisodicStore arg in WonderlandAgent. Base compose_context populates Context.relationships from relational notes for the trigger's speaker(s). All three layers are markdown-first per spec §8 — readable by humans, indexable for query.

tasks.title: Compaction-as-agent-behavior
tasks.details: Per WONDERLAND_SPEC §8: 'compaction is itself an agent behavior.' Hook on AgentMemory that triggers between threads (or on demand): the agent prompts itself in-character to reflect on the just-completed thread and produce semantic + relational distillations. Hatter's reflections are nonlinear; Caterpillar's are slow/categorical. For T16 we land the mechanism — a CompactionPrompt template, a hook on AgentMemory.compact(thread_id, llm), tests with mocked LLM. Per-character compaction prompts are stubs that subclasses override.
